newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana lawyer sees Congress regulating tobacco.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana lawyer sees Congress regulating tobacco.

text.p: Louisiana Attorney General Richard Ieyoub said Tuesday he believes Congress will draft legislation acceptable to states that will regulate the tobacco industry once the companies settle suits filed by individual states.

To be accepted by the states, Ieyoub said federal legislation must end the marketing tobacco products to children, require tobacco companies to fully disclose the health effects of smoking and establish federal regulatory oversight of the tobacco industry.
"These guys are slippery. We've got to make sure we nail them down in a legislative act," he said.

Ieyoub declined to comments on details of ongoing talks between the state attorneys general and the industry, citing a confidentiality agreement. He said those talks could resume as early as next week.

Speaking a day after the attorneys general involved in litigation against tobacco companies met in Chicago to discuss strategy, Ieyoub downplayed rumors that divisions are forming among the ranks of the state's top legal advisros.
"There is no such division," he said. "We firmly established a unity of purpose."
Ieyoub said tobacco companies will come under increased pressure to settle with the state attorneys general as the first of their state trials approaches in the coming months.
"It is my opinion that they would try to stave off litigation and get this thing settled," he said.
